* Fixes https://github.com/goshs-labs/goshs/security/advisories/GHSA-6m5c-fv2q-jrj2

The unauthenticated ConPtyShell.ps1 exemption in BasicAuthMiddleware and
InvisibleBasicAuthMiddleware only matched on the `conpty` query key and the
request path. It did not restrict the HTTP method and did not require `conpty`
to be the sole query parameter, so an attacker could append `?conpty` to reach
the full authenticated API surface anonymously (?bulk webroot read, ?goshs-info,
?ws, ?catcher-api, ?cbDown, ?embedded) and issue unauthenticated PUT/DELETE
writes — a critical auth bypass on servers started with -b/--basic-auth or
-ca/--cert-auth.

Scope the exemption to its intended use via a shared conPtyExempt() helper: a
GET/HEAD of exactly /ConPtyShell.ps1 whose only query parameter is `conpty`.
The generated upgrade URL (/ConPtyShell.ps1?conpty) still serves without
credentials; every other method or extra feature key falls through to auth.

Adds regression tests in middleware_test.go pinning the exemption boundaries
for both middlewares.

Fix/sftp goshs acl ghsa 2m7f (#279)

* Enforce per-folder .goshs ACL over SFTP (GHSA-2m7f-jq4x-rcj7)

The SFTP request handlers performed only a webroot-boundary check
(sanitizePath) and never consulted the .goshs per-folder ACL that HTTP
and WebDAV enforce. Any holder of the single, webroot-wide SFTP
credential could therefore read, write, list, rename, or delete files in
a directory that .goshs protects under a different credential or blocks
outright over HTTP — a full cross-protocol authorization bypass.

Add httpserver.ProtocolACL, an exported fail-closed ACL enforcer for
credential-less transfer protocols. It mirrors webdavEnforceACL /
aclFile.Readdir: because SFTP presents no per-folder basic-auth
credential, a non-empty .goshs "auth" is an unsatisfiable requirement and
is denied outright; block-listed names and the .goshs file itself (which
holds the bcrypt hashes) are denied; FilterListing hides .goshs, blocked
entries, and auth-protected subdirectories from directory listings.

Wire Allowed() into readFile/writeFile/listFile/cmdFile in
sftpserver/helper.go, including the Rename destination, and FilterListing
into directory listings. The design is deliberately fail-closed: an SFTP
client can never reach a folder guarded by a per-folder credential it
cannot present.

Regression tests in sftpserver/acl_test.go reproduce the advisory PoC
(read/write/list/stat/remove/rename denials, .goshs exposure, listing
filter) and confirm unprotected paths still work.

Fix/ghsa 8f9w 966j qhq9 (#304)

* Fix GHSA-8f9w-966j-qhq9: make auth lockout check-and-count atomic

verifyCredentials checked the per-IP failure counter and updated it in two
separate critical sections around the bcrypt compare, reusing a stale entry
pointer for the update. Concurrent wrong-password requests from a fresh IP
all passed the check and the stored count ended at 1, so the brute-force
lockout never triggered.

The attempt is now reserved (counted) in the same critical section as the
lockout check, before verification; requests beyond the budget (failures
plus in-flight attempts) are refused up front, and the failure path re-reads
the map to arm the lockout. A successful login still clears the record.
